title: Electrically Reversible Layer-Tensor Responses in Bilayers
authors: Zehou Li, Shenda He, Pan Zhou, Baoru Pan, Rui Tan, Lizhong Sun
abstract: The layer Hall effect provides a prototypical example of a hidden layer response in van der Waals bilayers: opposite layers carry compensating Hall currents at zero out-of-plane electric field, while an applied out-of-plane electric field $E_z$ selects one layer over the other and switches the net Hall response. Here we show that this field-switching mechanism is not restricted to Hall transport, but follows from a general symmetry principle for response tensors. We formulate a selection rule for the layer tensor effect (LTE) using Jahn symbols. For a tensor with Jahn symbol $J$ and rank $r$, the stacking operation that exchanges the two layers acts as a coset representative relating the $+E_z$ and $-E_z$ states. Tensor components that are odd under this operation are forced to cancel between layers at $E_z=0$, and acquire a macroscopic response satisfying $T_α(+E_z)=-T_α(-E_z)$. This criterion allows us to enumerate the symmetry-allowed electrically reversible tensor components associated with different Jahn symbols and to identify their physical realizations in common response tensors. We apply the theory to representative anomalous Hall, shift-current, nonlinear Drude, piezoelectric, spin Hall, and spin-photocurrent channels. Model calculations and first-principles simulations further confirm the predicted field-odd responses. Our results establish an electrically switchable LTE framework, providing a unified route to multifunctional layertronic responses in bilayer materials.
summary: This paper generalizes the concept of the layer Hall effect into a symmetry-enforced framework called the Layer Tensor Effect (LTE). It uses Jahn symbols and layer-exchange symmetry to derive a selection rule predicting that certain tensor components must vanish at zero electric field but exhibit a sign reversal when the field is reversed. This provides a unified theoretical route to designing multifunctional, electrically switchable responses in bilayer materials.
main_problem:
To generalize the layer Hall effect—where opposite layers cancel a response at zero out-of-plane electric field ($E_z=0$) but yield a switchable net response when $E_z 
eq 0$—to a general symmetry principle governing layer-resolved tensor responses, termed the Layer Tensor Effect (LTE).
main_result: The theory establishes a symmetry-enforced framework predicting electrically switchable responses in various transport channels, characterized by the layer-odd nature of the contributing tensor components.
method: The authors formulate a selection rule for LTE using Jahn symbols, based on the layer-exchange stacking operation ($\hat{\ell}$), which dictates that components odd under this operation must exhibit a sign reversal upon field reversal ($T_{\alpha}(+E_z) = -T_{\alpha}(-E_z)$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on van der Waals bilayers, which possess the layer index as a natural internal degree of freedom, and applies the theory to various response tensors like anomalous Hall, shift-current, and piezoelectric responses.
key_observables: The total response tensor components ($T_{\alpha}$), which are predicted to be antisymmetric under the reversal of the out-of-plane electric field ($\Delta E$).
important_parameters: The out-of-plane electric field ($E_z$ or $\Delta E$), which breaks the layer-exchange symmetry; the Jahn symbol ($J$) characterizing the tensor symmetry.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the layer-exchange stacking operation ($\hat{\ell}$) and assumes the existence of a layer-odd component that is allowed in the constituent layers.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the core mechanism: the response cancels at $E_z=0$ but becomes finite and switches sign when $E_z$ is applied and reversed.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept via the layer Hall effect, develops the general symmetry selection rule using Jahn symbols and layer parity, and then applies this theory to enumerate and predict switchable responses across multiple physical transport channels.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, symmetry-based theoretical tool to predict and classify novel, switchable electronic responses in 2D and multilayer materials, which is highly relevant for designing next-generation electronic devices.

(c) −Ez swaps the dominant and weak layers, reversing the sign, T tot α (−Ez) = −T tot α (+Ez).
